data.title: Middle East Eye: GCC to establish joint forward-command centre in Kuwait
data.author: Sean Mathews
data.summary:
GCC to establish joint forward-command centre in Kuwait
Submitted by
Sean Mathews
on
Tue, 11/10/2026 - 16:47
Given the intense attacks Kuwait has faced from Iran and its allies in Iraq, questions remain about how the new centre could be defended
Gulf Cooperation Council secretary general Jasem Mohamed al-Budaiwi gives a press conference with Russia's foreign minister and Bahrain's foreign minister after the 9th joint ministerial meeting of the strategic dialogue between the GCC and the Russian Federation in Manama, on 18 October 2026 (Fadhel Madan/AFP)
Off
The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) has approved a new joint forward-command centre to deepen military integration among members, as doubts rise about the US’s commitment to regional security amid the war on Iran.
The command centre will be built in Kuwait, a Gulf state that endured thousands of missile and drone strikes from Iran and Iraqi militias aligned with Tehran.
GCC secretary general Jasem al-Budaiwi said in a statement on Tuesday that the deployment of "appropriate" forces to the centre would take place, but did not provide additional details.
The GCC body representing six Gulf states established a joint defence agreement in 2000, stating that an attack on one member is an attack on all.
The GCC’s commitment to self-defence, however, is not as ironclad as that of the Nato military alliance.
The move could be seen as an effort to address the GCC's lack of a joint military command structure. The organisation has failed to respond to attacks on members from several fronts.
The GCC did not respond when Israel attacked Hamas negotiators in Doha, Qatar, in September 2025. The organisation has also failed to respond to devastating Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia.
The decision to base the command centre in Kuwait may also raise questions about its practical viability.
Kuwait’s geography at the hook of the Gulf made it especially vulnerable to missile and drone attacks from both Iran and Iraqi mili

data.title: Middle East Eye: F1 star Lewis Hamilton visits Gaza border
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
F1 star Lewis Hamilton visits Gaza border
Formula One star Lewis Hamilton visited Egypt's Rafah border crossing on Tuesday and met aid workers delivering assistance to the war-battered Gaza Strip, according to an Egyptian government statement.
North Sinai governor "Khaled Megawer took Lewis Hamilton on a visit to the Rafah land crossing to learn about the Egyptian efforts to support the Palestinian brothers in the Gaza Strip", the statement read.
Video shared by Megawer's office showed the seven-time world champion greeting aid workers and learning about their efforts to get supplies into Gaza, where this week heavy rains swept away tens of thousands of tents.
According to a truce struck by Israel and Hamas last year, at least 600 trucks of aid per day should enter Gaza, where more than two million people are facing a severe humanitarian crisis.
Aid workers say only a fraction of that amount is being allowed through by Israeli authorities, who control all entry into the territory.

data.author: Murad Idris

Submitted by

By attacking his motives, the senator-elect's opponents turned a debate over US funding for Israel's genocide in Gaza into a trial of his character
Abdul El-Sayed (left) won Michigan’s US Senate seat on 3 November, two days after Haley Stevens (centre), the Democrat he beat in the primary, endorsed his Republican opponent Mike Rogers (right) (Jeff Kowalsky, Jim Watson and Blake Fagan/AFP)
Off
In his victory speech last week, Abdulrahman El-Sayed, the first Muslim American elected to the US Senate, said "hate" or "hateful" five times, and each time the word did something different.
He recalled supporters asking why he never called his opponents hateful. Those opponents, he said, "hate the idea" of an America big enough for people who pray differently.
He told Mike Rogers, the Republican he had just beaten, "You chose hate, and Michigan chose hope." Then he turned to those who call people hateful for believing that Palestinian children should not be killed with American tax dollars: "That's not hate. It's love."
In one speech, Sayed declined the word "hate", turned it around, used it as a weapon and refused it as a name. The rhetoric of hate is the currency of American politics. It gets minted, exchanged and spent, and it buys moral standing, which converts into votes and endorsements .
Everyone trades in it, including the man it was aimed at, but its real value is sorting groups into those accused of hate and those who make the accusation.
Follow its circulation through Michigan. "Hate" hounded Sayed throughout his campaign. Rogers regularly denounced his "hateful ideology". One Democrat told CNN he could not vote for Sayed "because I'm against hate".

More than a million people have signed a petition urging Democrats to reject Hakeem Jeffries as the next Speaker of the US House of Representatives, as growing opposition to his leadership puts his support for Israel and US foreign policy under renewed scrutiny.
Jeffries, who currently leads the House Democrats, is expected to become the first Black speaker when the new Congress convenes in January, after the Democrats' sweeping midterm victories on 3 November.
But Jeffries is not the speaker-elect yet. He confirmed his candidacy last week, but his colleagues must elect him later this month. Jeffries stands currently uncontested, with no other Democratic lawmaker throwing their hat in the ring for the position.
While no one in the party has come forward to run against Jeffries, several newly elected lawmakers have voiced reservations about his policy positions, casting doubt on whether or not they will endorse him.
Some voters and influencers have mobilised, with dozens of viral videos urging citizens to call their representatives and sign the petition against Jeffries.
“We believe the Speaker should represent the Democratic voters, not just the Democratic establishment,” says the petition put forward by social media influencer Nicole Whitted.
The petition calls on representatives to examine Jeffries' public record, policy positions, campaign donor record, and leadership.

The force, whose mandate in Lebanon expires at the end of this year, said the patrol "was fired upon with about a dozen rounds" near Wadi Jilu and returned fire, after which the shooting stopped.

"We reiterate the obligation under international law for all actors to ensure the safety and security of UN personnel and property at all times," it said.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Analysis: The changing face of Israel’s ultra-Orthodox politics
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Analysis: The changing face of Israel’s ultra-Orthodox politics
ne of the most significant developments in the aftermath of the Israeli elections was the decision by United Torah Judaism (UTJ), the main ultra-Orthodox Jewish party, not to recommend Benjamin Netanyahu to form the next government.
This marks a departure from years of close alliance between Netanyahu and the ultra-Orthodox, or Haredi, parties, long considered a pillar of Israeli politics.
Even if the move was tactical, intended to strengthen the Haredi parties’ bargaining position, it sends an important signal, as last month’s vote exposed several significant shifts within Haredi society.
They include the declining standing of veteran political leaders, a struggle over the future of Haredi leadership, the emergence of a new political force challenging established conventions from within, and a deepening crisis surrounding the model of the “society of learners”.
The trauma of the Hamas-led 7 October attack may have bypassed the Haredi spiritual leadership and its veteran MPs, but the wider Haredi public, including the generally more conservative Lithuanian community, understands that something momentous has happened in Israel. This is particularly true of the younger generation.
